title: [observability][storage] A branch deleted under its mounted workspace is made again by the next checkpoint, from the workspace (on main; no main: no parent), recorded as artifact.branch_recreated; a commit that keeps failing is logged when it starts failing or fails another way, and once when it gets through, not on every pass
prompt:
Spawn, objective 205 [observability][storage] (the lead's ask of 2026-11-16, incident I-006; author rev-g; reviewers: rev-f, then rev-e as the second reviewer (owner t467u, 2026-11-17: no cc-astra)): a branch deleted under its mounted workspace is made again from the workspace, and recorded; a checkpoint that cannot commit is logged once per change, not on every pass.

Base: main 6f8ceb8c.

The problem (live, read-only trace in sync/queue.md, 2026-11-16):
- At 03:59 on 2026-11-15 the three refs of ws/.sources/scratch.git were deleted (the mirror for agents with no mission source). agent_supervisor's branch was one of them, and its workspace was mounted.
- A restarted loop (05:30:58, the deploy of 8adefdef) re-read the supervisor's transcript to a turn end. Its checkpoint ran crates/spawn-host/src/git.rs commit: `git rev-parse refs/heads/agent_supervisor` fails.
- The Bridge (crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs checkpoint, the WorkspaceError::Unavailable arm) pushed "commit unavailable: git rev-parse refs/heads/agent_supervisor: fatal: ambiguous argument ..." on every pass. That is about 4 a second: 66,430 lines from 04:10 to 12:21 on 11-15, and 193,529 on 11-16 before 13:30, three journal lines each, in a journal capped at 546 MB.
- A failed turn-end checkpoint holds its transcript line back, so the supervisor's transcript was not followed past that line: no turn or commit records since 11-15 05:31.
- Nothing makes the branch again: mount and ensure_branch run only at an execution's start.

What changes:
- Decided, with a default; reviewers and cc-astra may push back. A branch gone from the store while its workspace is mounted is made again by the next checkpoint, from the workspace.
  - R2 (rev-f's F2): in a mission's mirror whose source receives branches, spawn-cli sources.rs commit first takes the branch back from what this host published. restore_published lists the source's spawn/<agent> with ls-remote, fetches it into a private ref (refs/spawn-restore/<agent>, removed after), and creates refs/heads/<agent> from it only while it is absent (update-ref with the empty old value), so an existing branch is never moved. The checkpoint then goes on top of it, and its push is a fast-forward the integrator sees. The result is Commit::Recreated with that head as its parent; an unchanged workspace is Recreated at the head itself. Nothing published, or the branch made meanwhile, falls through to the store below. R5 (the lead, 2026-11-17, on R4's load failure) replaces R2's "a source that refuses or cannot be reached falls through": see R5 below.
  - spawn-host git.rs commit: when `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}` finds no branch, the new GitWorkspace::recreate builds the workspace's tree by the checkpoint's own rules (tree_of: files over the cap, runtime files and build output left out).
  - The commit's parent is the store's main head; with no main, the commit has no parent, and tree_of reads the empty tree as its head.
  - The ref is made with `update-ref <ref> <commit> ""` (made only while still absent, so a branch someone made meanwhile is never overwritten).
  - It returns the new Commit::Recreated { commit, parent } (spawn-core port.rs).
  - Why main and not the last checkpoint: the store keeps no record of it once the ref is gone (the reflog goes with the ref), and its objects may be pruned. On main, the branch's diff against main is exactly the workspace's work.
  - A made-again branch is published like a created one: sources.rs marks the pusher on Commit::Recreated too (rev-f's F2). On main or with no parent, if the source still holds an older spawn/<agent>, its push is refused as a rewrite and reported, never forced. main_merge.rs records a Recreated checkpoint of the markers like a Created one.
- The Bridge, on Commit::Recreated:
  - one warning: "<session>: branch <agent> was gone from its store; made again at <commit> from the workspace, on main <main>", or "with no parent (the store has no main)";
  - then the new event `artifact.branch_recreated {artifact: {project, branch, commit}, parent}` (spawn-core event.rs EventKind::ArtifactBranchRecreated; parent null with no main);
  - then the checkpoint's own `artifact.committed`, in that order (record_recreated).
- A failing commit (WorkspaceError::Unavailable, or a refusal other than WorkspaceStale) is still retried every pass, and its checkpoint stays due as before. It is logged only:
  - when it starts failing;
  - when it fails for another cause. R2 (rev-f's F1): the key, spawn-core bridge.rs failure_key, is the failure's kind (`unavailable`, or `refused <code>`) and its message's first line, with each run of seven or more hex digits replaced by `<id>`. update-ref names a fresh commit id every pass, and git add's later lines name the files it failed at;
  - once more when a commit gets through after it, as a note ("<session>: commit available again", printed by the loop as "spawn loop: ...", not as a warning).
  The state is Follow::commit_failed, per execution and in memory: a restarted loop logs a failure that is still there once more.
- WorkspaceStale keeps its own guard (follow.stale); it is untouched.
- R3 (rev-f's F2, n1 on R2): taken_back maps the store's commit after a take-back: a new commit is Recreated on the published head; nothing new is Recreated at the published head itself (commit and parent the same).
- R4 (rev-e's F1 on R3): record_recreated queues artifact.branch_recreated, and record_commit flushes it with the checkpoint's artifact.committed (queue_commit), so a log down at the first append loses neither; the next pass appends both.
- R5 (the lead's ruling, 2026-11-17): publishing a branch that does not descend from what was pushed is worse than a delayed checkpoint. Two cases are kept apart:
  (a) the source was read and spawn/<agent> is truly absent there (ls-remote works and lists nothing): restore_published is Ok(None) and the store makes the branch again on main, as before. Unit: sources.rs a_branch_gone_from_the_mirror_is_taken_back_from_what_was_published, "nothing published, None"; black box: 205.sh (3) and (4).
  (b) the source cannot be read: a directory source that is not a directory now (commit() checks it before the take-back), ls-remote fails, the fetch fails, or the ref is missing after the fetch. commit() returns WorkspaceError::Unavailable ("take <agent> back from what was published: ..."); the branch is not made, the checkpoint stays due and is tried every pass, logged once per cause (R2's failure_key). Unit: the same test's gone source is an error and leaves no branch, and, in a_published_ref_the_source_cannot_send_is_an_error_and_reads_as_away, so is a published ref the source cannot send (listed, not fetched), which reads as away until a take-back gets through; black box: 205.sh (2c) and (2d).
  The bound: a source that stays unreadable is raised by the existing source_away alert (no new kind), at the second alert reading in a row that finds it away, so within two SPAWN_ALERT_CHECK_SECS (default 30 s, about a minute). source_away now reads a source as there only when it is a directory, `git ls-remote --heads -- <source>` works, and no take-back failed to fetch from it in the last 120 s (a failing take-back is tried every pass, so the mark stays while it fails; one that gets through, or reads nothing published, clears it) (sources.rs source_readable, TAKE_BACK_FAILED; unit a_source_is_there_only_when_git_can_read_it: a bare repository there, a plain directory and a missing path away). source_away is an alert, not a notice: it is in Needs you and in the supervisor's digest (SourceAway, whose text now says "or not one git can read"). One ls-remote per watched source per alert reading, on a local path.
- R6 (rev-g, 2026-11-17, on R5's load failure: 205.sh (1) under load made the branch again on main beside a published head): the take-back's check came before the store's lock. A pass that found the branch, then waited for the lock while the branch was deleted, reached the store with the branch gone, and the store made it again on main; its push was refused as a rewrite. The take-back is now asked by the store under the branch's lock: GitWorkspace::commit_or_take_back(workspace, message, take_back) calls take_back only when the branch is gone, then reads the branch again: made, the commit goes on it as on any branch; still absent, recreate as before; an error from take_back is the commit's, and nothing is written. WorkspaceStore::commit is commit_or_take_back with a take-back that does nothing. sources.rs commit() passes the directory check and restore_published as the take-back, and taken_back() wraps the result as before. Unit: spawn-host tests/api.rs a_take_back_is_asked_under_the_lock_only_when_the_branch_is_gone (not asked when the branch is there; its error leaves no branch; what it makes is the parent). Deterministic (the lead's ask on R6): sources.rs commit_routed (MissionWorkspaces::commit's work on the routed store, with no database) calls a cfg(test) pause, before_store_commit, right before the store; sources::tests::a_branch_deleted_on_the_way_to_the_store_is_still_taken_back deletes the branch there and needs Recreated on the published commit, never main. R5's order (whether the branch is there read before the store's lock: rev-g's check-before-lock mutant) fails it. Black box: 205.sh (1) under load.

Read first:
- crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs: checkpoint, record_commit, Follow;
- crates/spawn-host/src/git.rs: commit, tree_of, track_runtime_files, source_commits;
- crates/spawn-core/src/port.rs: Commit;
- crates/spawn-core/src/event.rs: EventKind, name();
- crates/spawn-core/src/memory.rs: commit;
- crates/spawn-cli/src/commands/loops.rs: how warnings and notes are printed.

Tests (unit; no existing test changes its assertions):
- spawn-host tests/api.rs a_branch_deleted_under_its_mounted_workspace_is_made_again_from_the_workspace: on main; the next checkpoint is an ordinary one; with no main, a commit with no parent; the workspace's files in both.
- R2 tests:
  - spawn-core tests/branches.rs a_commit_failure_is_reported_once_per_cause: one cause at two files is one line; the same refusal with a fresh id is one line; a second cause is a second line; then the note. Also a_failure_key_masks_ids_and_reads_the_first_line.
  - spawn-cli sources.rs a_branch_gone_from_the_mirror_is_taken_back_from_what_was_published: nothing published, None; published, the pushed head; an existing branch never moved, and no private ref left; a source that is gone, None.
  - spawn-host tests/api.rs, in the re-create test: a branch ref that exists but is no commit (written by hand) is refused, never overwritten (the empty old value; rev-f's mutant).
  - MemoryStore::fail_commits_saying is a new test helper.
- spawn-core tests/branches.rs:
  - a_failing_commit_is_reported_once_until_it_gets_through: one warning, five quiet retries, one note when it gets through, reported again after a new failure;
  - a_branch_made_again_by_a_checkpoint_is_recorded_before_the_checkpoint: MemoryStore::lose_branch, a new test helper.
- Two exhaustive matches in spawn-host's tests gain the Recreated arm.

The scenario rsi/scenarios/205.sh (black box; 179.sh's world: a real `spawn loop`, one ephemeral worker on a fake engine; the mission's source is a scratch repository that receives branches; BB:WRITE <name> writes a file into the workspace):
  (1) one.txt's checkpoint published, the branch deleted from the mirror, a turn: within 20 s the branch is back with the workspace's files, its parent the published head. artifact.branch_recreated names it and that parent, and an artifact.committed of it is recorded. The source's spawn/<agent> reaches it. The loop logged one "was gone" line and no "commit unavailable".
  (2) the next turn: an ordinary checkpoint on it.
  (2b) R3: a take-back with nothing new is recorded at the published head.
  (2c) R5: the source moved away and an empty directory in its place (a directory git cannot read), the branch deleted, a turn: once the loop has logged it (30 s at most, its passes are slower under load) and 3 s more, the branch is still absent, exactly one new "commit unavailable" saying it could not be taken back from what was published, and a source_away alert fired (only git's reading finds it away); the empty directory removed: once logged and 3 s more, still absent and one more line, saying the source is not a directory now; the source moved back: the branch is taken back from what was published, and its new commit is on it.
  (2d) R5: the source's spawn/<agent> written by hand as an id it has no object for (ls-remote lists it, the fetch fails), the branch deleted, a turn: once logged and 3 s more, still absent, one more "commit unavailable", and a new source_away alert; the ref mended: taken back on what was published.
  (3) nothing published, the branch deleted, a turn: made again on main, recorded, published.
  (4) nothing published and no main, the branch deleted, a turn: made again with no parent (event parent null), published.
  (5) the object store made unwritable, a turn: 12 s later exactly one "commit unavailable"; a file written into the workspace that git add now fails at first (the same cause, other later lines): still one; then the store writable but the branch's ref locked (another cause; update-ref names a fresh commit each pass): 8 s later exactly two.
  (6) the lock gone: the work is on the branch, an artifact.committed of it, one "commit available again" note, and still two "commit unavailable".
  (7) the branch's ref written by hand as a blob's id, a turn: the ref is never written over (by the take-back or the re-create), and one more "commit unavailable".
  (8) R4: the log made to refuse artifact.branch_recreated (a constraint on the scenario's own database), the branch deleted ((7)'s checkpoint is still due, so no turn; the session's records, its turn ends too, wait behind the refused one): the branch is made again and nothing recorded; the constraint dropped: within 10 s an artifact.branch_recreated names the made-again commit and an artifact.committed of it is recorded (R3's code loses the artifact.committed: rev-g's r3-code mutant).
  The end checks that no background job of the script outlives it (the 179/193 fold's check).
The base (main 6f8ceb8c) exits 1 at (1): the branch is not made again.

Not in this objective: the live remedy for I-006 (the lead's, lead-mac's decision); deleting refs (the in-use check is I-006's follow-up).
